mainTopic: מעמד שלשתן as a rule without a stated reason, its limits, and the רב–שמואל dispute about sending money through a messenger (הולך)
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation for why a debt can be handed to a new creditor when all three people are present (מעמד שלשתן): the borrower gains from switching lenders, so he commits himself to the new one. That explanation falls apart with harsh creditors like the house of בר אלישיב, so מר זוטרא instead lists מעמד שלשתן among three rules the רבנן made like הלכה without a stated reason. Stories about רב's saffron show that such a transfer cannot be taken back, and that it works even for a small gift. In the story of the gardeners, רב נחמן first holds a gardener to his promise. After רבא's objection he agrees that a קנין made by mistake is undone. Next, רב and שמואל argue about someone who tells a messenger, "Bring a מנה to so-and-so, which I owe him": both say the sender is still responsible for loss, but they disagree about whether he can take the money back. The גמרא traces their argument to מיגו and brings a ברייתא supporting רב, which רבי זירא explains for the case of a deposit. The amud ends with a story about רב ששת's cloak money and begins another about רבי אחי's silver vessel, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The borrower commits himself because of the benefit he gets
steps.stepSummary: The explanation for מעמד שלשתן: the borrower gains from switching from an old loan to a new one, so he fully commits himself to the new lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the benefit the borrower gets when his debt switches from an old loan to a new loan, he fully commits himself to the new lender.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an explanation (given in רב אשי's name) of why מעמד שלשתן works. The borrower willingly binds himself to the new lender because he benefits from the switch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a debt cannot just be handed to someone else by talking. This explanation says the transfer works because the borrower agrees: a new lender might give him more time to pay. So the borrower's own commitment is what makes the new creditor's claim valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit, gain
Old loan (owed to the first lender)
New loan (now owed to the new lender)
He obligates himself, binds himself

phrases.english: With that benefit
that it changes for him
phrases.notes: "Him" is the borrower, and "it" is his debt.

phrases.english: from an old loan to a new loan,
he fully resolves and obligates himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of מעמד שלשתן begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעמד שלשתן works because the borrower, who benefits from the switch, willingly binds himself to the new lender.

steps.title: What about creditors who give no extra time?
steps.stepSummary: הונא מר בריה דרב נחמיה asks רב אשי about harsh creditors like the house of בר אלישיב. The borrower gains nothing from them, so would the transfer fail?
steps.simpleTranslation: הונא מר בריה דרב נחמיה said to רב אשי: If so, take people like the house of בר אלישיב, who tie up debtors and collect immediately. Would the transfer not work with them?!
steps.whatsHappening: A challenge to the benefit explanation. It points to tough creditors who never give extra time, so the borrower would not want to switch to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the transfer works only because the borrower gains something, then where he gains nothing it should not work. The house of בר אלישיב grab their money right away, so the borrower gets no benefit. The challenge asks whether the transfer really fails in such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then... (introduces a problem with what was just said)
They tie up
Immediately
They acquired

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הוּנָא מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחֶמְיָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Huna Mar son of Rav Nechemya said to Rav Ashi:
If so,
such as those of the house of Bar Elyashiv,
who tie up debtors and take payment immediately,
would they also not acquire?!
phrases.notes: He means: when the debt is moved over to these harsh people, does the transfer simply not work?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the benefit explanation from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מעמד שלשתן works because of the borrower's benefit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With harsh creditors the borrower gains nothing, so by this reasoning the transfer should fail. That seems wrong.

steps.title: Then the rule would depend on circumstances
steps.stepSummary: Agreeing that the transfer fails with harsh creditors is not acceptable either, because the rule would then depend on each case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that yes, indeed it does not work with them, then you have made your rule depend on measurements!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenger blocks the easy way out. Saying "the transfer just doesn't work there" creates a new problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תקנה of the רבנן is supposed to be one clear rule for everyone. If it worked only where the borrower gains, every case would need to be checked on its own. That makes the rule unworkable, so the benefit explanation cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (heads off a possible answer)
Yes indeed, so too
You have made your words depend on measurements, so the rule is no longer fixed

phrases.english: And if you say, yes, indeed,
if so, you have given your words over to measurements!
phrases.notes: The rule would change from case to case instead of being one fixed rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off the possible answer to the challenge in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible reply that the transfer really fails with harsh creditors
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reply would make a fixed rabbinic rule depend on each case's details, which is unacceptable.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: three rules made like הלכה without a reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the benefit explanation and quotes מר זוטרא. מעמד שלשתן is one of three rulings the רבנן made like הלכה without giving a reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר זוטרא said: These three matters the רבנן made like a הלכה, without a reason. One is this (the transfer when all three are present).
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא shows the גמרא is giving up the earlier explanation. Instead it says מעמד שלשתן is simply a fixed rule with no reason given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no logical reason survives the challenge, the גמרא says the transfer works because the רבנן set it up that way, like a הלכה למשה מסיני. Because it does not rest on the borrower's benefit, it works the same with every creditor, even harsh ones. That solves the problem from steps 2 and 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Three matters
The רבנן made them
Like a fixed הלכה, without a stated reason

steps.whatToRemember: מעמד שלשתן works because the רבנן set it as a fixed rule. It does not depend on whether the borrower gains, so it applies to every creditor.
steps.confusionAlert: "Without a reason" does not mean the rule is random. It means it does not depend on a reason, so it applies the same way in every case.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because there is no reason to check case by case, the transfer works with every creditor.

phrases.english: Rather, Mar Zutra said:
These three matters
the Rabbis made them like a halacha without a reason:
One is this;
phrases.notes: "This" is the case we've been discussing: handing over a debt when all three people are present.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the benefit explanation that steps 2 and 3 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces a reasoned explanation with a fixed rabbinic rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעמד שלשתן works because the borrower benefits and so commits himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעמד שלשתן is a rule the רבנן made like הלכה without a reason, so it works in every case.

steps.title: Second rule: writing all property to one's wife makes her only a manager
steps.stepSummary: The second of the three rules: someone who writes all his property to his wife makes her only a manager of it, not its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another is what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: One who writes all his property to his wife has made her only a manager.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא lists the second rule the רבנן made without a stated reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the gift seem to give the wife full ownership. Still, שמואל rules that she only becomes the one who looks after the property. This is accepted as a fixed rule, without the reason being explained.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the next item on the list)
One who writes over all his property
Manager, steward of the property

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידַּךְ – דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And another is what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
One who writes all his property to his wife,
has made her only a manager;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ – דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in מר זוטרא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who writes all his property to his wife makes her a manager of it, not its owner.

steps.title: Third rule: the eldest son married in the house acquires it
steps.stepSummary: The third rule: if a father marries off his eldest son and the wedding is held in the house, the son acquires that house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another is what רב חנניה said: One who marries off a woman to his eldest son in the house, the son has acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא finishes his list of three rules with רב חנניה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No formal act of acquiring takes place. Even so, the son becomes the owner of the house where his wedding was held. This is the third rule the רבנן set without a stated reason.

keyTerms.meaning: One who marries off (arranges a wife for someone)
His eldest son
He acquired it

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא's three rules made without a reason: (1) מעמד שלשתן, (2) all property written to a wife makes her a manager, (3) the eldest son married in the house acquires it.

phrases.english: And another is what Rav Chananya said:
One who marries off a woman to his eldest son
in the house, the son has acquired it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the house where the wedding took place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and last item in מר זוטרא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An eldest son whose father marries him off in the house acquires that house.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מעמד שלשתן belongs to a group of three rules the רבנן made like הלכה without a stated reason.

steps.title: רב hands over his saffron in the third person's presence
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רב אחא ברדלא to give a קב of saffron he owes רב to someone else, saying it in front of that person so that רב cannot take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רב אחא ברדלא: You are holding a קב of saffron that belongs to me. Give it to so-and-so. I am saying this to you in front of him so that I will not be able to take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing רב using מעמד שלשתן: the owner, the one holding the item, and the receiver are all present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב moves his saffron to a third person with words alone, with no act of קנין. He makes a point of saying it in the receiver's presence, and adds that this way he will not retract. That added phrase is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: A קב, a unit of measure
Saffron
In his presence (literally, before his face)
To go back on a statement, to retract

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב אַחָא בַּרְדְּלָא:
phrases.english: Rav said to Rav Acha Bardela:
I have a kav of saffron with you;
give it to so-and-so.
I am saying this to you in his presence
phrases.notes: "His presence" means the presence of the person receiving the saffron.

phrases.english: so that I will not retract it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב אַחָא בַּרְדְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the list of the three rulings, the גמרא brings a story of רב applying מעמד שלשתן himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item held by another person can be moved to a third person by instruction given in the presence of all three.

steps.title: Does this mean that without saying it he could retract?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רב's words that if he had not spoken in front of the receiver, he could have retracted. That would make מעמד שלשתן weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we learn from this that if he wanted to retract, he would be able to retract?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב's statement. If רב had to add "so that I will not retract," it sounds like retracting is normally possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's words seem to say that being in front of the receiver is what stops him from retracting. That suggests that in other cases a giver could go back on the transfer. Such a reading would contradict the fixed rule that מעמד שלשתן fully works.

keyTerms.meaning: From the implication, by inference
Is able, can

phrases.english: By inference, if he wanted to retract,
he would be able to retract?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of רב's phrase "so that I will not retract."
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding a reason why he cannot retract implies that retracting would otherwise be possible, which would make מעמד שלשתן reversible.

steps.title: רב was explaining the rule, not adding a condition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב: he was saying that statements made in the presence of all three can never be taken back.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: These kinds of statements cannot be retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by explaining what רב really meant. He was telling רב אחא the הלכה: once it is said in front of the receiver, it cannot be undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question read "so that I will not retract" as a special step that blocks retraction. The answer reads it as a description of the law itself: מעמד שלשתן can never be retracted. That is why רב said it in front of the receiver.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant
Were not given to be retracted, cannot be taken back

phrases.english: This is what he meant:
These statements were not given to be retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inference by rereading רב's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's phrase was a special safeguard, implying that retraction is normally possible.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was stating the law: statements made in מעמד שלשתן can never be retracted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that מעמד שלשתן is final once said. The giver cannot go back on it.

steps.title: רב already taught this with the מנה case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need this story when רב already ruled that "I have a מנה with you, give it to so-and-so" works with all three present.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב already said this once! For רב הונא said in the name of רב: If someone says, "I have a מנה in your hand, give it to so-and-so," and all three are present, the receiver acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב's saffron case is needed, since רב already taught the same rule about a מנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rule from the same אמורא seems to appear twice. The גמרא assumes nothing is repeated without a reason, so it asks what the saffron case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: One time, once already
A sum of one hundred (zuz/dinars)
When all three people are present together
He acquired it

phrases.english: But Rav already said this once;
for Rav Huna said that Rav said:
"I have a maneh in your hand,
give it to so-and-so,"
in the presence of all three, he acquired it!
phrases.notes: The three are the owner, the person holding the money, and the receiver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the meaning of רב's statement and now asks why it was needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to record רב's saffron case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב already taught מעמד שלשתן with the מנה case, so the saffron story looks like a repeat.

steps.title: The saffron case teaches that small gifts also need all three present
steps.stepSummary: From the מנה case we might think only a large gift needs the receiver present. The small saffron gift teaches that it needs this too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we had only that case, I would have said this applies only to a large gift, but a small gift would not need to be done in his presence. So the saffron case teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the saffron story adds. A מנה is a large sum and a קב of saffron is a small one, so the story shows the rule holds for small gifts too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought a small gift could be moved by a simple instruction, without the receiver present. רב's saffron case shows that even a small gift needs the receiver present. The two cases together show the rule is the same for every size of gift.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (an early, mistaken assumption)
A large gift
A small gift
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: מעמד שלשתן works for any size of gift, and it always requires the receiver to be present. Once done, it cannot be retracted.
steps.confusionAlert: The early idea (הוה אמינא) was not that a small gift cannot be given at all. It was that a small gift would not need the receiver present. The גמרא rejects that idea.

phrases.english: If from that one alone, I would have said
phrases.notes: "That one" is the מנה case from the previous step.

phrases.english: this applies only to a large gift,
but a small gift
would not need to be in his presence,
phrases.notes: "His presence" means the presence of the receiver.

phrases.english: it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the rule was repeated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a large gift like a מנה needs the receiver present. A small gift could be moved by instruction alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a small gift like a קב of saffron needs מעמד שלשתן, so the rule is the same for every size of gift.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule does not change with the value of the gift.

steps.title: The gardeners settle accounts
steps.stepSummary: Some gardeners do their accounts. One of them is told, in front of the landowner, to give the extra five coins to the landowner, and the landowner makes a קנין with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were some gardeners who did their accounts with each other. Five coins were left over with one of them. The others told him, 'Give them to the landowner.' They said it in front of the landowner, and the landowner made a binding קנין with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. It is setting up a real case that will test the rule of מעמד שלשתן we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This looks just like מעמד שלשתן: the one holding the money, the one he owes, and the one who will receive it are all present. On top of that, there is also a formal קנין. So the deal seems doubly binding.

keyTerms.meaning: Gardeners, workers who farm someone else's land
An accounting, a calculation of who owes what
A type of silver coin
The owner of the land
Made a קנין with him, a formal act that makes a commitment binding

phrases.english: There were certain gardeners
who did a calculation with each other.
Five isterei zuzei were left over
with one of them,
they said to him: 'Give them to the owner of the land'
in the presence of the owner of the land,
and he made a קנין with him.
phrases.notes: The landowner did a formal act with the gardener that locks in the gardener's promise to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ גִּינָּאֵי דַּעֲבֻיד חוּשְׁבָּנָא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case of מעמד שלשתן, after steps 7–11 set the rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: money is assigned to the landowner in front of all three parties, and a קנין is made.

steps.title: The gardener finds he owes nothing, and רב נחמן says the deal stands
steps.stepSummary: The gardener checks his math again and finds he owes nothing. רב נחמן says he can't help him, because of רב's rule and because of the קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Later the gardener did the math by himself and found that nothing was left over with him at all. He came to רב נחמן. רב נחמן said: What can I do for you? First, there is the rule רב הונא said in the name of רב. And besides, they made a קנין with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. The gardener wants out of the deal, and רב נחמן rules that he is stuck with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן gives two reasons. First, רב's rule says a transfer made in front of all three parties can't be taken back. Second, there was also a formal קנין, which binds him anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Nothing at all was left with him
What can I do for you? (I can't help you)
First... and besides: two separate reasons

phrases.english: In the end he went
and did the calculation by himself,
and nothing at all was left with him.
He came before רב נחמן.
He said to him: What can I do for you?

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב.
phrases.english: First, because רב הונא said in the name of רב.
phrases.notes: This is the rule from the steps before: a transfer made in front of all three parties can't be taken back.

phrases.english: And besides, they made a קנין with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֶיעְבֵּיד לָךְ? חֲדָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and gives רב נחמן's first ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The transfer is binding, both through מעמד שלשתן and through the קנין.

steps.title: רבא objects: the gardener says the money was never his
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the gardener isn't refusing to pay a debt. He is saying there was never any money with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Is this man saying 'I won't give'?! He is saying 'it isn't with me'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule stops someone from backing out of a real obligation. Here the gardener isn't backing out. He is saying the whole thing was based on a wrong calculation, so neither רב's rule nor the קנין should hold him.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a strong objection)
I will not give
It isn't with me; I don't have it

phrases.english: רבא said to him:
Is this man saying 'I won't give'?!
He is saying 'it isn't with me'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the gardener is bound
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being bound by a deal assumes there was real money owed. The gardener's claim is that there was none, so this isn't a case of backing out at all.

steps.title: רב נחמן agrees: a mistaken קנין is undone
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן accepts רבא's point. The קנין was made by mistake, and any mistaken קנין is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: If so, it is a קנין made by mistake, and any קנין made by mistake goes back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן accepts the challenge and changes his ruling. The gardener does not have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we see that the gardener never owed the money, the קנין was built on a false fact. A deal made on a mistake has no force, so it is cancelled. This applies to the מעמד שלשתן transfer too.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that's the case
A קנין made by mistake
Goes back; is undone

steps.whatToRemember: מעמד שלשתן and a קנין both bind a person to a real obligation. But if the whole deal rested on a mistake, such as a wrong calculation, it is cancelled.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
it is a קנין made by mistake,
and any קנין made by mistake goes back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן agrees with רבא's objection.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A קנין made by mistake is undone, so the gardener does not have to pay.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about sending a debt through a messenger
steps.stepSummary: Someone tells a messenger, 'Bring a מנה to so-and-so, which I owe him.' רב says the sender is responsible if it is lost but cannot take it back. שמואל says that because he is responsible, he can take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Someone said, 'Bring a מנה to so-and-so, which I owe him.' רב said: The sender is responsible for it. And if he wants to take it back, he cannot. שמואל said: Since he is responsible for it, if he wants to take it back, he can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a dispute between רב and שמואל about money sent to a creditor through a messenger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the sender must pay again if the money is lost on the way, because it hasn't reached the creditor yet. רב still says he can't take it back. שמואל says the opposite: since the money is still the sender's responsibility, it is still his, so he can take it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring, deliver: an instruction to a messenger
A sum of one hundred דינרים
He is responsible for it; he must pay again if it is lost
Since; because of

steps.confusionAlert: רב and שמואל agree that the sender is responsible. They only disagree about whether he can take the money back.

phrases.english: It was stated:
'Bring a מנה to so-and-so, which I owe him,'
רב said: He is responsible for it;
phrases.notes: If the messenger loses the money, the sender still owes the debt and must pay again.

phrases.english: and if he wants to take it back, he cannot.
And שמואל said: Since he is responsible for it,
if he wants to take it back, he can.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הוֹלֵךְ מָנֶה לִפְלוֹנִי שֶׁאֲנִי חַיָּיב לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the gardener story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the sender is responsible but cannot take it back. שמואל: since the sender is responsible, he can take it back.

steps.title: Maybe they disagree whether 'bring' is like 'acquire'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב and שמואל disagree about whether saying 'הולך' gives the receiver ownership right away, the way 'זכי' does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they disagree about this: one master (רב) holds that 'bring' is like 'acquire', and one master (שמואל) holds that 'bring' is not like 'acquire'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to find the root of the argument between רב and שמואל from step 16. It suggests one possible reason they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'הולך' works like 'זכי', the messenger takes the money for the receiver right away, so the sender can no longer take it back. That fits רב. If 'הולך' is not like 'זכי', the money still belongs to the sender until it arrives, so he can take it back. That fits שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggestion that is often rejected.
They disagree
'Bring' or 'deliver': an instruction to carry something to someone
'Acquire': an instruction to take ownership for someone right now

phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about this:
that one master holds that 'bring' is like 'acquire',
phrases.notes: The first 'master' is רב, who said the sender can't take the money back.

phrases.english: and one master holds that 'bring' is not like 'acquire'?
phrases.notes: This 'master' is שמואל, who said the sender can take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes the reasoning behind the dispute in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle explains the dispute between רב and שמואל?

steps.title: No, they disagree about using a מיגו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Both agree that 'הולך' is like 'זכי'. They really disagree about whether we apply a מיגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that 'bring' is like 'acquire'. Here they disagree about this: one master (רב) holds we do not say 'since', and one master (שמואל) holds we do say 'since'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the suggestion from step 17 and gives a different reason for the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is: since the sender is still responsible if the money is lost, maybe he should also be able to take it back. שמואל accepts this 'since' reasoning. רב does not, so the money already belongs to the receiver and cannot be taken back.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
'Since': reasoning that because one thing is true, another follows
We say, meaning we apply this reasoning

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the usual court-claim מיגו, where someone is believed because he could have made a better claim. Here it means: since he still carries the risk of loss, he should also be able to take the money back.

phrases.english: No; for everyone agrees
that 'bring' is like 'acquire',
and here they disagree about this:
one master holds we do not say 'since'.
phrases.notes: This is רב: even though the sender still carries the risk, he can't take the money back.

phrases.english: And one master holds we do say 'since'.
phrases.notes: This is שמואל, matching his words in step 16: since he is responsible, he can take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 17 and gives a new basis for the dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the argument depends on whether 'הולך' is like 'זכי'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sides can agree that 'הולך' is like 'זכי'. The argument is better explained as a disagreement over the מיגו.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that in four cases of 'bring' or 'give' a מנה, whether as a debt or as a deposit, the sender is responsible for loss but cannot take the money back. This is exactly רב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא like רב: 'Bring a מנה to so-and-so, which I owe him'; 'Give a מנה to so-and-so, which I owe him'; 'Bring a מנה to so-and-so, a deposit he has with me'; 'Give a מנה to so-and-so, a deposit he has with me'. In all these, the sender is responsible for it, and if he wants to take it back, he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב's ruling word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling 'responsible for loss, but cannot take it back' is the same as רב's ruling in step 16. It covers both a debt and a deposit, and both the words 'bring' and 'give'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with his view
A sum of one hundred coins
A deposit: something left with a person for safekeeping
Responsibility for loss
Takes back, or changes his mind

steps.whyThisMatters: A ברייתא backing one side carries extra weight, so רב's position is strengthened here.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with רב:
'Bring a מנה to so-and-so, which I owe him';
'Give a מנה to so-and-so, which I owe him';
'Bring a מנה to so-and-so:
a deposit that he has with me';
'Give a מנה to so-and-so:
a deposit that he has with me':
he is responsible for its loss,
and if he comes to take it back, he cannot take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports רב's side of the dispute.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling: responsible for loss, but cannot take it back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with four cases (debt or deposit, 'bring' or 'give').

steps.title: With a deposit, the owner didn't want it handed to someone else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the deposit case: the sender should be able to say the owner never wanted his deposit given to someone else, so the transfer doesn't count.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a deposit, let him say to him: the owner does not want his deposit to be in someone else's hands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one part of the ברייתא: the deposit cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who leaves a deposit trusts that specific person, not a stranger. So handing it to a messenger is not something the owner agreed to. If so, the messenger never properly held it for the owner, and the sender should be able to take it back.

keyTerms.meaning: His wish, here the owner's wish
In someone else's hands

phrases.english: A deposit: let him say to him:
phrases.notes: The sender is speaking to the messenger, trying to get the money back.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁיְּהֵא פִּקְדוֹנוֹ בְּיַד אַחֵר!
phrases.english: It is not his wish that his deposit be in someone else's hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the deposit cases in the ברייתא from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that with a deposit, the sender cannot take it back.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner of a deposit does not want it in a stranger's hands, so the messenger's taking it should not count for the owner.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the sender is known as a denier
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that the ברייתא is talking about a sender who is known as a כפרן, so the owner is glad to have his deposit taken out of his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: it is a case where he is known as a denier.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question from step 20 by limiting the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the owner wants his deposit to stay with the person he chose. But if that person is known for denying what he owes, the owner would be happy for anyone else to hold it. So the sender cannot claim the owner objects, and he cannot take the money back.

keyTerms.meaning: Is known as, or has a set reputation
A denier: someone who denies money he owes

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports רב: the sender is responsible but cannot take it back. For a deposit, this applies where the sender is known as a כפרן.

phrases.english: רבי זירא said:
When he is known as a denier.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the sender who was holding the deposit, so the owner would be glad to get it away from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner of a deposit never wants it in another's hands, so the sender could take it back.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the sender is known as a כפרן, the owner prefers the deposit to be anywhere else, so the transfer counts and the sender cannot take it back.

steps.title: רב ששת sends רב יוסף בר חמא to collect his cloak money
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת was owed money for cloaks in מחוזא. He asked רב יוסף בר חמא to bring it. The merchants asked רב יוסף to make a קנין taking responsibility, and he said yes, but in the end he slipped away without doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת was owed money in מחוזא for cloaks he had given merchants to sell. He told רב יוסף בר חמא: when you come back, bring the money to me. רב יוסף went there and the merchants gave him the money. They said to him: let us make a קנין with you, so that you take responsibility for it. He told them: yes. But in the end he slipped away from them without doing the קנין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a real-life story about money sent through a messenger. Here it only sets up the facts; רב ששת's reaction comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף was sent by the receiver, רב ששת, to collect the money. The merchants wanted a קנין so that he would be formally responsible for what he received. He agreed out loud but never actually made the קנין, so he took on no formal obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: A credit: money owed to someone under a set agreement
Cloaks
Let us make a קנין with you, a formal act that binds you to responsibility
He slipped away, avoided them

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet had
a credit of cloaks in Mechoza.
phrases.notes: Merchants in מחוזא sold his cloaks for him and owed him the money.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא:
phrases.english: He said to Rav Yosef bar Chama:
When you come back, bring them to me.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the money the merchants owe.

phrases.english: He went, and they gave it to him.
phrases.notes: Literally 'they gave them to him': the merchants handed the money to רב יוסף.

phrases.english: They said to him: Let us make a kinyan with you;
He said to them: Yes.
In the end, he slipped away from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת הֲוָה לֵיהּ אֲשַׁרְתָּא דְּסַרְבָּלֵי בְּמָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא about sending money through a messenger, the גמרא brings a real-life case of a messenger collecting money for the receiver.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A messenger sent by the receiver agreed to take responsibility through a קנין but never actually made the קנין.

steps.title: רב ששת praises רב יוסף for not taking on responsibility
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tells רב יוסף he did well not to make himself like a borrower who is a slave to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יוסף came to רב ששת, רב ששת told him: You did well. You did not make yourself into the 'borrower who is a slave to the lender'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת reacts to the story and approves of רב יוסף slipping away without making the קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By avoiding the קנין, רב יוסף did not tie himself to the merchants with a debt-like responsibility. רב ששת uses the פסוק to show that taking on such an obligation for no reason makes a person like a slave. So the messenger did the right thing by staying free of it.

keyTerms.meaning: You did well
The borrower is a slave to the lender (משלי 22:7)
You made yourself into

phrases.english: When he came to him,
phrases.notes: רב יוסף came back to רב ששת.

phrases.english: he said to him: You did well,
that you did not make yourself
"the borrower is a slave to the lender."
phrases.notes: משלי 22:7

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא לְגַבֵּיהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שַׁפִּיר עֲבַדְתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב ששת's reaction to the story told in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A messenger does well not to take on needless responsibility through a קנין.

steps.title: Another version: the merchants are the borrowers
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב ששת says 'You did well', reading the פסוק as being about the merchants, who are his borrowers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: רב ששת said, You did well, because 'the borrower is a slave to the lender'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב ששת's words, using the same פסוק in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'borrower' is not רב יוסף but the merchants who owe רב ששת money. Since they are the borrowers, the responsibility should stay on them until the money reaches him. So רב יוסף was right not to take that responsibility off them.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same story or statement

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions quote the same פסוק, but they point it at different people. In the first version the 'borrower' would have been רב יוסף. In the second, the 'borrowers' are the merchants.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions רב ששת approves of רב יוסף not making the קנין. They differ only in how the פסוק 'עבד לוה לאיש מלוה' is applied.

phrases.english: Another version:
You did well;
"the borrower is a slave to the lender."
phrases.notes: This time the merchants are the borrowers, so the responsibility stays on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב ששת's reaction, reading the same פסוק differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The merchants, as the borrowers, stay responsible for the money until it reaches the lender.

steps.title: A new story begins: רבי אחי's silver vessel in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a second story: רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה had a silver vessel in נהרדעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחי the son of רבי יאשיה had a silver vessel in נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new story about property held in another city. The rest of the story continues after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only gives the background: who owned the item, what it was, and where it was. It prepares another real case about getting property back through someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver vessel
נהרדעא, a city in Babylonia

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַחַי בְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה הֲוָה לֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Achai the son of Rabbi Yoshiya had
a silver vessel in Neharde'a,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַחַי בְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה הֲוָה לֵיהּ אִיסְפְּקָא דְכַסְפָּא בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second story on a related subject, right after the רב ששת story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background only: רבי אחי owned a silver vessel located in נהרדעא.
